title: Clinical feasibility of two cardiac deep learning cine magnetic resonance imaging sequences: Single-breath-hold and free-breathing motion-corrected approaches.
summary: Deep learning accelerated cine sequences are compared with conventional segmented cine in 86 patients, with scan time reduced by about 62-73% and comparable function measures, a clinical feasibility result where the DL reconstruction is the enabling method. The conclusion is limited to the reported study setting. Published in Journal of Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance.
